messages.content: Return exactly one JSON object, with no prose or Markdown, using only the requested keys and exact requested labels or expressions.

This JavaScript function should return the first index whose value is greater than or equal to x: function lowerBound(a, x) { let lo = 0, hi = a.length; while (lo < hi) { const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2); if (a[mid] <= x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; } return lo; }. For the sorted array [1,2,2,4,7], return defect_label using the exact label upper_bound_condition, corrected_comparison using the exact expression a[mid] < x, index_for_2, index_for_3, and index_for_5.

Five deliveries J, K, L, M, and N occupy distinct slots 1 through 5. K is immediately after J. M is after K. N is before J. M is immediately before L. Return the unique order as an array, plus the one-based slots of J, M, and N.

Inspect this Python function intended to return the largest sum of any contiguous window of exactly k items: def best_window(values, k): current = sum(values[:k]); best = current; for i in range(k, len(values)): current += values[i] - values[i-k+1]; best = max(best, current); return best. Return defect_label using exact label outgoing_index_shift, corrected_update using exact expression current += values[i] - values[i-k], and result_for_4_1_7_2_6_k3.
Return exactly one JSON object, with no prose or Markdown, using only the requested keys. All amounts are integer cents.

An account starts at 24,000 cents. Apply these events in order: debit 3,750; credit 1,280; debit 2,415; credit 935. A 125-cent fee applies after each debit only when the post-debit balance before the fee is below 20,000. Return final_balance, debit_total excluding fees, credit_total, fee_count, and fee_total.
